# Duckpad 0.12.0
Run a terminal alongside your documents, with Ghostty embedded in Duckpad.
- Open the terminal from the status bar or View menu. The bundled Ghostty 1.3.1 engine renders real login-shell sessions; a separate Ghostty installation is not required. - Create independent session tabs with Command-T. Tabs follow the editor’s multiline tab layout, and the previous eight-session limit is removed. - Split right with Command-D or down with Command-Shift-D, navigate panes, equalize sizes and toggle split zoom. Each session supports up to sixteen panes. Terminal layout undo is separate from document undo and retains closed panes for five seconds. - Terminal focus uses Ghostty’s macOS default bindings for supported terminal actions. Editor focus restores Duckpad’s editor shortcuts. Terminal search, command filtering and the engine inspector are available. - Right-click a session tab to close tabs to its left or right, close other tabs, or close all tabs. Close confirmation includes a persistent “Don’t ask again” option; the context menu can turn confirmation back on. The trailing add/hide header buttons are removed. - Screen changes synchronize the render layer’s backing scale and framebuffer dimensions. Font zoom and window resizing update the shell’s terminal dimensions through Ghostty’s IO thread. First-time split creation keeps both panes visible.
App and helpers: **0.12.0 (58)**. Requires **macOS 13 or later**. Universal binaries support Apple Silicon and Intel. Existing document formats, recovery, settings and native plugin ABI remain compatible.
## Installation
Download `Duckpad-0.12.0-universal.dmg` and drag Duckpad into Applications, or extract `Duckpad-0.12.0-universal.zip`. Verify the downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The signed Sparkle update feed is published after the release archive is uploaded.
## Scope and limits
The editor retains its App Sandbox. An authenticated, unsandboxed terminal XPC helper starts `/bin/zsh -l` and owns each process lifetime; shell commands can access files with your user account’s permissions. The engine initializes only when a terminal is first requested.
Terminal processes are not restored after quitting the app. Custom shell selection and full terminal accessibility are not implemented. Terminal mouse forwarding currently supports the left button and scrolling; right/middle-button TUI gestures are not supported. Terminal appearance defaults to a dark palette. Duckpad’s terminal configuration is separate from the standalone Ghostty app’s configuration. OSC clipboard access is disabled; explicit copy/paste remains available.
The default build is ad-hoc signed, without Developer ID signing or Apple notarization. Physical Intel hardware, macOS 13 and live Korean IME have not been exercised. The original external-to-Retina scale problem was reproduced, but final external-display round trips remain unverified because only the built-in Retina display was connected for the final preview checks.
## Validation
All 34 focused Swift tests pass. Terminal tests cover session creation and removal, tab wrapping, close routing, bulk-close cancellation and undo, confirmation persistence, command filtering and first-split geometry. Native Apple Silicon preview checks cover shell execution, font zoom, window resizing, first splits and close UI. PTY integration checks cover exec failure, UTF-8, working directory, resizing, Ctrl-C and process exit. All eight localization catalogs pass key and format validation; new close UI was inspected in English.
The universal app and all three helpers pass architecture, version, resource, dependency-license and signature checks. Isolated packaged-app checks pass Finder/Open With, bookmark recovery and saving after relaunch, native save-access renewal, window resizing and sandboxed XPC isolation. A continuously writing shell closes successfully within the five-second shutdown budget (0.4 seconds in the release validation run).
